item.title: ILT20 Season 5 introduces new batter zone Wide rule and two-way 60-second stop clock
item.description: The upcoming fifth season of the International League T20 will feature significant changes to its playing conditions, with a new "batter zone" to determine Wide deliveries and the extension of the 60-second stop clock to the batting side. The revised regulations, which come into effect from the opening match on November 21, aim to ensure greater consistency in umpiring decisions and maintain a faster pace of play. The introduction of the batter zone marks one of the biggest changes. Under the new rule, a delivery will be called Wide if the entire ball passes outside the designated zone between the off-side and leg-side wide lines at the popping crease. A delivery passing above the standing batter’s head height will also be deemed a Wide. The rule will apply even if a batter moves across the crease to reach the delivery, provided no part of the ball passes within the designated zone and the batter makes no contact. An exception will apply to reverse sweeps and switch hits, for which the existing off-side Wide lines will be used. Another notable change concerns the 60-second stop clock, which will now apply to both batting and fielding teams. Previously enforced only on the fielding side, the regulation requires both batters to be ready for the next over within 60 seconds of the previous over ending. Teams will receive two warnings per innings. From the third offence onwards, the fielding side will be awarded five penalty runs. Certain situations, including injury treatment, strategic time-outs, weather interruptions and third-umpire reviews, will be exempt. The playing conditions also strengthen opportunities for regional cricketers. Each Playing XI must include at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one player from an ICC Associate Member nation. This minimum combination must be maintained during substitutions and Super Sub changes, with specific provisions for concussion replacements. The fifth edition of the tournament will run from November 21 to December 20, 2026, featuring six franchises and several prominent international players.

item.title: Anthony Davis Reportedly Wants To Return To Lakers, But A Reunion Is Unlikely
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Brad Mills-Imagn Images Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis spent five and a half seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers , and it appears he might want a reunion. Brian Windhorst recently appeared on ESPN LA’s The Sedano & Kap Morning Show , where co-host Scott Kaplan told him he’d overheard reporters in the media room at a Lakers game talking about Davis wanting to come back to Los Angeles. “They don’t realize I’m listening and I’m hearing what they’re saying,” Kaplan said. “[One of them said], ‘I hear that Anthony Davis wants to return to the Lakers.’… I think they’re credentialized. I think they know what they’re talking about. They assume I have no idea. But Windy, could Anthony Davis… We always talk about another big man for the Lakers. “A, have you heard it?” Kaplan continued. “And B, is there a world where that could happen?” Windhorst rightly pointed out that Kaplan was talking about gossip in the press room. As for whether Davis and the Lakers could reunite, the 48-year-old doesn’t see it happening. “Very unlikely,” Windhorst said. “Anthony Davis is one of the bigger question marks in the league this year. There’s like three guys we’re watching, sort of star-level players about will they get traded. One is Anthony Davis, one is Kyrie Irving, Domantas Sabonis is on there. All of them are in the same boat. “All of them have options in their contract for next season,” Windhorst continued. “… The Wizards basically said, ‘We want to see Anthony Davis play 20 to 30 games, see how he fits with our group, and then we’re going to revisit about whether we want to give him a contract extension.’ Obviously, if they give him a contract extension, he agrees to it, he’s not being traded. “If he doesn’t get a contract extension, then I think you’re going to see his name out there on the trade market,” Windhorst added. “But here’s the thing. item.description: The Dylan Larkin trade saga has taken another interesting turn, and the Boston Bruins remain a team worth watching. While the Detroit Red Wings continue searching for an acceptable return for their former captain, a source has floated a potential trade framework involving veteran center Pavel Zacha , defenseman Mason Lohrei , or a first-round draft pick. There is a catch, of course. Actually, there are several. According to reporting from James Murphy of The Sick Podcast , Boston has been pushing harder to enter the Larkin sweepstakes. However, the Bruins reportedly have no interest in surrendering prized young center James Hagens, a player Detroit is believed to covet. That raises an obvious question: Could Boston satisfy the Red Wings without sacrificing one of its most promising young players? Oct 22, 2026; Boston, Massachusetts, USA; Boston Bruins center Pavel Zacha (18) skates with the puck during the third period against the Nashville Predators at TD Garden. The source wondered whether Zacha, accompanied by Lohrei or a first-round selection, could provide enough value to get Detroit interested. Importantly, this was a hypothetical framework raised by a source, not confirmation that Boston has submitted such an offer . Still, the names are worth examining. Zacha, 29, is an established NHL center who could immediately help fill the enormous hole Larkin would leave behind. He also carries some risk, considering he is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent following the 2026-27 season. item.title: Maresca ‘concerned’ after Man City suffer third league loss in a row
item.description: Manchester City Coach Enzo Maresca gives an interview prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League soccer match between RB Leipzig and Manchester City at Red Bull Arena. (is associated with: «Maresca ‘concerned’ after Man City suffer third league loss in a row») Jan Woitas/dpa Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is concerned about his side’s form after they suffered a third Premier League defeat in a row by going down 3-1 at Nottingham Forest. City won their opening seven games of the season but followed up defeats to Aston Villa and Brighton with a poor reverse at the City Ground. They were 2-0 down inside 18 minutes as Jair Cunha and Liam Delap scored before Rayan Cherki’s fine strike after the break gave them hope. But Delap’s second on the counter-attack killed the game and left Maresca’s side six points off leaders Arsenal. “I’m always concerned, even when we win games,” the Italian said. “We need to have balance. We won seven in a row. Now we have lost three in a row, so we need balance on that." “During the international break, try to understand what we can do better, and try to start again after the international break." “In the same way we have done the first one, we’re going to use this international break to try to clarify what we can do better," he addded. “We know we do some things better, and also we know we need to improve things. So we are going to use that and try to understand how we can avoid these kind of games,” he continued. Maresca revealed Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were replaced at half-time due to injury. “Both injury, both asked for a change,” he said. “Marc Guehi an injury. Josko Gvardiol had some issue already during the week, so it was just because they had problems.” The victory could be a coming of age for Delap and Forest, who have struggled to adapt to life under new boss Oliver Glasner, with just one win from their opening nine games. Delap had scored once in eight games following his club-record move from Chelsea, but his brilliant double proved he can be the man to fire Forest to better things this season. “It’s now for Liam to keep working, getting into his best shape,” Glasner said. “Let’s say getting back to the Liam Delap he has been at Ipswich, and then even of course improving his game and he has still a lot to improve. “Definitely not his finishing with left and right, but he has to improve his heading, he has to improve his movements in the box. “He has to improve his understanding what we’re doing out of possession. But, also very honestly, he did very well.” Glasner reacted to Delap’s second goal with a touchline sprint to join in the celebrations. The Austrian said: “Of course, I can’t demand from the players they have to outrun the opposition, and I run less than the opposite manager. So I think I had to follow. “I just was told they were running six or seven kilometres more than City today, and that means I had to run more than Enzo Maresca as well, and I did my job. It was funny for me.”

item.title: Indiana Pacers Can Now Afford To Sign A Free Agent. Should They?
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 02: Quenton Jackson #29 of the Indiana Pacers makes a move on Corey Kispert #24 of the Atlanta Hawks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on November 02, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty Images INDIANAPOLIS – The Indiana Pacers can now afford to sign a veteran 15th player to their roster. But do they need to do it right now? That’s the question the team’s front office is considering. Entering the season, the Pacers team spending level was over the luxury tax line and, of all importance for their roster size, near the first apron. That first apron acts as a hard cap for Indiana because they used a specific salary cap exception to sign wing Kelly Oubre in the offseason. When the season began, the Pacers had $206.8 million committed in terms of guaranteed contracts and possible salary bonuses. The first apron is just over $209 million. That left the team with a bit over $2.2 million in space between their roster spending and their hard cap. The veteran’s minimum for the entire 2026-27 NBA season is just shy of $2.45 million. That meant the Pacers couldn’t even afford to sign a player to a minimum-salary agreement when the season began – only a player with zero (and drafted in the second round) or one year of service could have been added to their team at the time. As a result, the Pacers carried 14 players on their roster to begin the season. But once the regular season starts, every passing day makes minimum contracts cheaper. They pro-rate based on how much of the season remains. And so earlier this week, a veteran’s minimum contract became small enough in remaining value that the Pacers could afford to sign any available free agent to a one-year contract. But the question remains: Should they? Entering the season, the answer to an early-as-possible addition seemed like it should be no. Just because the Pacers could sign someone doesn’t mean they should. Because minimum contracts pro-rate, as noted above, every passing day gives the Pacers more flexibility. For example, if the team opted to sign a player on the first possible day they could have, and that player stayed with the team for the rest of the season, the Pacers (essentially) couldn’t take back more salary than they sent out in trades or signed a player to a 10-day contract if they opened a roster spot – among many other transactions that would have become harder or impossible by using (basically) all of their remaining apron space at the first possible instant. The Pacers can – if they’re able to keep avoiding a signing – keep more team-building avenues open by waiting. Between slightly imbalanced trades, short-term signings, and other considerations related to their Mid-Level Exception, there are plenty of reasons to wait. item.title: Chiefs Get Triple Injury Blow on Defense Before Week 9 Clash With Jets
item.description: Cornerback Mansoor Delane logged 27 tackles and an interception across five starts, while rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods added 13 tackles and a half-sack in seven games to anchor Kansas City’s defense. Behind their contributions, the Chiefs built a top-tier run defense, allowing just 96.3 rushing yards per game this season. However, following a frustrating loss to the Denver Broncos, Kansas City now faces a sudden depth crisis. The latest defensive injuries force Kansas City to shuffle its personnel ahead of the matchup against the New York Jets. Mansoor Delane and two others miss Jets clash due to injuries Heading into Week 9, the Kansas City defense faces a sudden roster crunch as official injury reports confirm three key starters will sit out the upcoming matchup against New York. Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane (5) celebrates with defensive end George Karlaftis (56) after a play against the Seattle Seahawks during the first half of the game at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Chiefs confirmed the status in their Week 9 update: “Nikko Remigio is questionable to play Sunday against the New York Jets. Peter Woods, Mansoor Delane, and Omarr Norman-Lott are out,” the team announced . Woods is dealing with a neck injury, Delane has a shoulder issue and Norman-Lott is listed with a knee injury. Andy Reid said Woods and Delane are progressing, but neither will play Sunday. “Both those two… are making progress, and that’s a positive thing, but they’re going to be out this game. It’s just a matter of getting back and making sure they’re strong; both of them, it’s a strength thing right now,” Reid said. Delane’s absence removes a first-round corner from the secondary. Kansas City selected the LSU product sixth overall in 2026. He has one interception and five pass breakups. Woods was also a first-round pick. His 13 tackles, half-sack, and pass breakup have supported the interior rotation. Norman-Lott’s absence further reduces the rotation and places more work on Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga. Remigio has 274 yards on 10 kick returns and 70 yards on 12 punt returns, giving Kansas City field-position value. The Chiefs enter after a 28-24 loss in Denver, their second defeat of the season after a 5-0 start. They allowed 11 penalties for 105 yards, and personal fouls helped Denver score 18 points. Sunday’s game at Arrowhead will test Steve Spagnuolo’s rotation. The Chiefs need replacements to protect the run defense, limit big plays, and avoid short fields. Their communication will matter against a Jets offense that has scored 58 points since Week 7. item.title: 'A shared vision': LASA boys pace each other to Class 5A UIL state cross-country title
item.description: The LASA boys team, flanked by Stacia Crescenzi, LASA's principal and assistant coach Sarah Davis on the left and head cross country coach Mary Beth Metcalf and assistant coach Kitty Kistler on the right, stand on the podium after winning the Class 5A state championship at the UIL state cross-country championships at Old Settler's Park in Round Rock, Texas. (Brom Hoban/Special to American-Statesman) ROUND ROCK - Over two cool, breezy days at Old Settler's Park, more than 1,500 of the state's best high school distance runners competed in the UIL state cross-country championships. And while there were a number of standout performances from Central Texas runners, it was Austin's LASA Raptors who rose to the pinnacle, capturing first place in Saturday's Class 5A race. The Raptors were led by senior Liam Brandyberry, who finished seventh overall in 15 minutes, 28 seconds on the rolling 5K course. "It took preparation, drive, commitment, character and courage to do what they had to do today, which is not easy," LASA head cross-country coach Mary Beth Metcalf said of the boys team, which also consisted of seniors Joaquin Gonzalez, John Wilson, Cruz Alcorta and Hugo Radjef, and juniors Ben Vazquez and Sam Smith. "Not so much a tactical approach, it was more about being committed to one another," Metcalf added. "During the race, when it feels overwhelming, when they feel like maybe they can't hang on any longer, when their brains are telling them to let up, I ask them to think about one another and the love that they have for their teammates, and to let that teammate commitment be what drives them forward. Our team has a shared commitment and obligation to will it into reality. It's a shared vision." Only the top five runners from each team have their finishing places added together to calculate the team score; the team with the lowest total score wins. LASA scored 94 points, ahead of runner-up Weslaco East's 98 and third-place Dallas Wilson's 113. Weslaco East's Alexander Nava won the overall race in 15 minutes, 13 seconds, while Georgetown's Matthew Morales averaged 4:56 per mile to grab second in 15:18. Liberty Hill's Zander Radziwon was 11th (15:40) and Lockhart's Ethan Herrera (15:52) was 19th. "These boys, since they've been freshmen, they've always felt like a team and worked together like a team," LASA principal Stacia Crescenzi said. item.title: Serie A probable line-ups: Napoli vs. Lazio
item.description: Serie A probable line-ups: Napoli vs. Lazio Serie A leaders Lazio are forced to do without Mattia Zaccagni, but rely on Davide Frattesi and Gustav Isaksen, while Napoli hope Kevin De Bruyne, Scott McTominay and Rasmus Hojlund can end the crisis. It kicks off at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples on Sunday at 11.30 GMT (12.30 CET). Few expected the two teams to be in their current position going into the season, as Gennaro Gattuso’s Lazio are alone three points clear at the top of the table, where Max Allegri is facing calls for his dismissal after a series of poor results, including the 4-1 Champions League defeat to FC Porto. PORTO, PORTUGAL – NOVEMBER 04: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, looks on before the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Porto and SSC Napoli at Estadio do Dragao on November 04, 2026 in Porto, Portugal. (Photo by Diogo Cardoso/Getty Images) The injury crisis keeps on getting worse for Napoli , as Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Leonardo Spinazzola, Stanislav Lobotka, Benoit Badiashile, David Neres, Alisson Santos, Costantino Favasuli and Alessandro Buongiorno are ruled out. Luca Marianucci is also suspended following his red card in last week’s 2-0 Serie A defeat to Juventus, with Mathias Olivera not at 100 per cent. This leaves extremely limited options, so Allegri has two major choices to make over his tactical set-up. Like his fellow drivers, Verstappen had to wait almost an hour and a half because of the red-flag delay before he could even get out on track. Asked how he had spent that time during the heavy rainfall, Verstappen laughed in front of Viaplay's camera: "Watching football. Premier League." item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams Hit With NFL Fines
item.description: The Detroit Lions picked up a hard-fought 19-15 victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8, but two of their biggest offensive stars are now paying a price for their actions during the game. On Saturday, the NFL announced that wide receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams were each fined $11,941 for taunting during Detroit’s November 1 victory at Ford Field. That’s a combined $23,882 in fines for the Lions’ dynamic receiving duo. Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams (1) reacts to a penalty after a first down celebration against Minnesota Vikings during the first half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Detroit Lions Receivers Fined for Taunting According to the NFL’s official accountability report , both violations occurred during the first quarter. Amon-Ra St. Brown: $11,941 for taunting with 11:25 remaining in the first quarter. Jameson Williams: $11,941 for taunting with 4:55 remaining in the first quarter. Williams’ penalty came following a 46-yard reception from Jared Goff that moved Detroit deep into Minnesota territory. However, the receiver was flagged after spinning the football near a Vikings defender, costing the Lions 15 yards. St. Brown was penalized earlier in the quarter after standing over a Minnesota defender following a running play. Both incidents resulted in unsportsmanlike conduct penalties during the game. Jameson Williams Has Been Here Before Interestingly, this isn’t the first time Williams has found himself dealing with the NFL’s disciplinary process this season. Earlier in the year, Williams was assessed fines totaling $26,867 for taunting and an illegal celebration during Detroit’s Week 2 loss to Buffalo. However, the receiver successfully appealed both fines , resulting in those penalties being rescinded. Whether Williams or St. Brown will appeal their latest fines remains to be seen. Despite the penalties, Detroit ultimately got the result it wanted against Minnesota. As we previously reported following the victory , Williams caught the go-ahead touchdown pass from Goff in the fourth quarter, helping the Lions hand the Vikings their first loss of the season. The victory also improved Detroit’s record to 5-2, with the Lions leaning heavily on a rushing attack that piled up 230 yards . The NFL has made it clear that taunting violations can carry consequences beyond the field. For St. Brown and Williams, that lesson now comes with a combined $23,882 price tag, assuming the fines are upheld.

item.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold watches from the bench as Fede Valverde scores a stunner from right-back for Real Madrid
item.description: Valencia CF v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Trent Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid to become their first-choice right-back, but under Jose Mourinho he is now watching a midfielder do that job instead. Captain Fede Valverde started there again at Mestalla and smashed in the opener against Valencia, while Alexander-Arnold and summer signing Denzel Dumfries were left out of the starting XI once again. Valverde strikes from right-back at Mestalla Valverde lined up at right-back for Real Madrid's trip to Valencia on Saturday, with neither Alexander-Arnold nor Dumfries in Mourinho's starting XI. The Uruguayan made the call look inspired in the 28th minute, when Kylian Mbappe's free-kick was blocked by the wall and the ball rolled back to the Real Madrid captain. Valverde controlled the ball around 20 metres out and drilled a powerful low strike into the net. Arda Guler doubled the lead eight minutes later, and the visitors went in at the break 2-0 up. Captain dominates in an unfamiliar role Valverde's display was about far more than his goal. According to Sofascore, he had 32 touches in the first half, completed 26 of his 29 passes and was not dribbled past once, while Real Madrid enjoyed 75 per cent of possession. It was the latest sign that Mourinho's experiment has become a settled plan. Valverde was first moved to right-back during the 1-0 win over Villarreal last month and has since started there against Sevilla, RB Leipzig and Barcelona, as well as at Mestalla. Alexander-Arnold's minutes dry up The shift has hit Alexander-Arnold hardest. The England international has played just 435 minutes in all competitions this season, with only four starts in La Liga, and he was an unused substitute in Real Madrid's last three Champions League games. His only start since the Villarreal game came in the 3-0 win at Racing Santander , when Valverde missed out with muscular discomfort. It is a sharp fall for a player who made 30 appearances last season despite a string of injuries, while Dumfries has also lost his place only months after arriving. What next for the sidelined full-backs? Real Madrid had won seven games in a row in all competitions before kick-off, so Mourinho has little reason to change a winning side. Speaking at his press conference before the Racing game, he insisted: "In the end, everyone will play." Alexander-Arnold can count on England. Thomas Tuchel left him out of his World Cup squad but has since recalled him, and he played 90 minutes in both wins over the Czech Republic during the last international break. England face Croatia on Thursday.

item.description: McLaren's British driver Lando Norris celebrates after securing pole position for the Sao Paulo Formula One Grand Prix (Nelson ALMEIDA) McLaren's outgoing world champion Lando Norris grabbed pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix with a brave and well-judged drive in Saturday's rainswept qualifying at Interlagos. The 26-year-old Briton clocked a best lap in one minute and 27.470 seconds to outpace George Russell of Mercedes by 0.204 seconds as heavy rain curtailed Q3 at the end of a session that lasted almost two and a half hours. "It's been a great qualifying, to be on pole again here, two years in a row! Different conditions to last year, but I am very happy. "It was about getting two laps in and not making a mistake and that is exactly what we did so it has been a very good day." Russell was disappointed not to take pole after being told by Mercedes to ease off on his final push lap. "Congrats to Lando, but it was definitely my pole lap. We should have finished the lap."
